problem: Audio-visual navigation (AVN) work focuses on policies and memory, while the audio-visual fusion module stays a simple concatenation or attention gate. This leads to single-modality dominance, information degradation and weak cross-domain generalization.
motivation: Humans combine hearing and vision seamlessly, but agents often have modality imbalance or domain discrepancy. The authors observe that fusion behaves differently across environments: vision dominates in clean synthetic Replica scenes, while audio-visual complementarity matters in noisy Matterport3D scenes. A robust, adaptive fusion is therefore needed.
key_idea: Fuse audio and visual features through a shared bidirectional residual interaction vector, scaled by learnable small-initialized per-modality coefficients, with LayerNorm and tanh for stabilization.
insight: Removing the Fusion Controller (LN + learnable residual scales + tanh) drops Replica Heard SPL from 76.7 to 69.3 and SR from 93.1 to 84.9, and Matterport3D Heard SPL from 57.3 to 53.1. The learned residual coefficients also reveal environment-dependent modality reliance: beta_a shrinks on Replica, giving a visually dominated policy, while both stay balanced on Matterport3D. The initialization beta_init=0.2 works best; 0.1 and 0.3 are worse, notably on Matterport3D (SPL 53.2 and 53.3 vs 57.3).
method: Encoders: visual (depth or RGB) and binaural audio spectrogram are encoded separately into v_t and a_t.
Bidirectional residual interaction: non-linear maps U_v and U_a project both features to a shared space, and h_interact = 0.5(U_v(v)+U_a(a)) serves as a shared residual signal for both streams.
Fusion Controller: v_hat = tanh(LN(v) + beta_v*h_interact), a_hat = tanh(LN(a) + beta_a*h_interact), with learnable scalars beta_v and beta_a initialized small (0.2 best).
Policy: fused features go into a GRU followed by an Actor-Critic head, trained end-to-end with PPO on top of the SoundSpaces codebase.
Modal dependence analysis: the trajectories of beta_v and beta_a during training are visualized to interpret modality reliance.

setting.backbone: SoundSpaces-style CNN encoders + CRFN fusion + GRU Actor-Critic (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces audio-visual navigation on Replica (18 scenes) and Matterport3D (85 scenes); 102 sounds, of which 78 train / 11 val / 18 test for the unheard setting; 40k PPO updates on Replica and 60k on MP3D
setting.action_space: discrete low-level (move forward, turn left, turn right)

numbers_note: The split is not stated explicitly; test is inferred from the text (unheard sounds are used for test scenarios). RGB results are not reported. The ablation tables also list a Matterport3D Unheard w/o FC row (SPL 28.9, SR 37.7), which beats the full model on SPL.
results: CRFN beats the SoundSpaces baseline on Replica and Matterport3D, in both Heard and Unheard settings. Replica Heard SPL/SR are 76.7/93.1 vs 74.4/91.4, and Unheard SPL is 41.6 vs 34.7. On MP3D Heard SPL/SR are 57.3/70.3 vs 54.3/67.7. SNA on Replica Heard is slightly lower than SoundSpaces (47.3 vs 48.1).
limitations: Only the Depth setting is evaluated, and the only baselines are the original SoundSpaces methods; there are no recent AVN methods or RGB results.

The modality-dependence claim rests on beta curves and a plausible explanation, without controlled causal tests. The paper's own claim of best performance across all metrics is contradicted by Replica Heard SNA, and the MP3D unheard ablation is mixed.
Gains are modest, single-run numbers with no variance reported.
